assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and made inequality of opportunity empirically tractable at exceptional scale.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are a coherent core for the research programme; the contribution combines major data construction with an influential explanatory empirical framework.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated a large and durable research agenda, with methods and findings extensively used in public and labour economics.
uncertainties: The broader collaborative programme makes any three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work provided a compelling account of how trade and technology shocks reshape local labour markets, tasks, and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a clear central group for the linked empirical and conceptual contributions.
assessment.maturity: Its consequences for labour-market research and policy debate have been tested over a substantial period and remain highly consequential.
uncertainties: Separating the distinct contributions of trade, automation, and other labour-demand changes remains empirically difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence methods supplied unusually direct evidence on labour-market discrimination and reshaped empirical work on unequal treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially central to the canonical correspondence-study contribution; Charles is a defensible additional credit for the broader field.
assessment.maturity: The designs are now foundational, widely replicated, and influential far beyond labour economics.
uncertainties: Audit designs identify treatment at particular margins and do not by themselves resolve all mechanisms or the prevalence of discrimination across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony made imperfect competition central to understanding wages, employer power, and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning provides the most identifiable intellectual centre, while Ashenfelter and Naidu represent important empirical and modern extensions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a durable organizing principle and has stimulated extensive empirical measurement.
uncertainties: The breadth of the field and the differing nature of theoretical and empirical contributions complicate a compact award attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory and measurement of adverse selection in insurance fundamentally improved how economists diagnose information problems in major insurance markets.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie represent a coherent combination of influential empirical measurement and theoretical guidance.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is well established and has been applied broadly in health, credit, and insurance economics.
uncertainties: Selection, moral hazard, and institutional design can be difficult to distinguish empirically in individual applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation established childhood as a critical economic period with long-run consequences.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are central to evidence on health and early shocks, while Cunha is central to the dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: A broad body of evidence and a sustained policy-relevant literature support the importance of the contribution.
uncertainties: The listed contribution joins related empirical and theoretical strands whose precise boundaries are broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation offered a powerful framework for connecting firm-level distortions to aggregate productivity and international income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central to the prominent measurement framework, with Restuccia an important contributor to its development and interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively adopted in growth and development research and has produced a substantial follow-on literature.
uncertainties: Empirical distortion measures can embody modelling assumptions, and the causal sources of measured misallocation remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible analysis of persistent outcomes feasible in many settings where unobserved heterogeneity and endogeneity are central.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond provide the core method, and Blundell is integral to the system-GMM development.
assessment.maturity: These methods have been used for decades across applied economics and their strengths and limitations are well understood.
uncertainties: Widespread application has also revealed sensitivity to instrument proliferation and specification choices.
